message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.  
The example is written in two ways:

| Method | What you run | Why you might choose it |
|--------|--------------|------------------------|
| **`gcloud` CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Quick, interactive, automatically handles authentication. |
| **REST API (curl)** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/...` | Useful if you’re building a programmatic workflow or integrating with another system. |

> **Important** – Before you run either example you must:
> 1. Enable the **Compute Engine API** for your project.  
> 2. Enable the **NVIDIA GPU Driver** installation (the instance will need the driver installed after boot).  
> 3. Make sure you have the **`gcloud` SDK** installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> 4. Replace the placeholder values (`PROJECT_ID`, `ZONE`, etc.) with your own.

---

## 1. `gcloud` CLI – One‑liner

```bash
# Replace these placeholders
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=install_gpu_drivers.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What the flags mean

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` is a good starting point. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `nvidia-tesla-a6000` is the RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 100 GB. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Runs a shell script at first boot (see below). |
| `--tags` | Optional network tags for firewall rules. |

### `install_gpu_drivers.sh`

Create a file named `install_gpu_drivers.sh` in the same directory as the command:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA GPU drivers (required for RTX A6000)
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
sudo reboot
```

> **Tip:** The driver version (`535`) may change; check the [official NVIDIA driver list](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-downloads) for the latest compatible driver.

---

## 2. REST API – `curl` example

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), use the following `curl` command. Replace the placeholders accordingly.

```bash
# Set variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)

# JSON payload
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
EOF

# POST request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

### Explanation

- **`machineType`** – Full resource path for the machine type.  
- **`accelerators`** – Adds the RTX A6000 GPU.  
- **`disks`** – Boot disk from the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family.  
- **`metadata.startup-script`** – Installs the NVIDIA driver and reboots.  
- **`tags`** – Optional network tags for firewall rules.

---

## 3. Post‑Creation Checklist

| Step | Command / Action | Why |
|------|------------------|-----|
| **Verify GPU availability** | `gcloud compute accelerator-types describe nvidia-tesla-a6000 --zone=$ZONE` | Ensure the GPU type is available in your zone. |
| **Check instance status** | `gcloud compute instances describe $INSTANCE_NAME --zone=$ZONE` | Confirm the instance is running and the GPU is attached. |
| **SSH into the instance** | `gcloud compute ssh $INSTANCE_NAME --zone=$ZONE` | Verify the OS and GPU driver installation. |
| **Test GPU** | `nvidia-smi` | Should show the RTX A6000 and driver version. |

---

## 4. Common Pitfalls & Tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **GPU quota exceeded** | Request a GPU quota increase in the GCP console. |
| **Instance fails to start** | Check the serial port logs (`gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output`). |
| **Driver not installed** | Ensure the `startup-script` runs correctly; you may need to add `sudo apt-get install -y software-properties-common` before adding the driver PPA. |
| **Firewall blocking traffic** | Add firewall rules for the tags you used (`http-server`, `https-server`). |

---

### TL;DR

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=install_gpu_drivers.sh
```

That’s all you need to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine instance** with an **RTX A6000 GPU** running **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**. Happy GPU computing!
